content:
Activity: Disciple-Leadership Paper



Answer the following questions about the mini-case and disciple-leadership: 

Why did Henri’s story and subsequent commitment have such a dramatic and immediate impact on the leaders who reported to him?: Henry’s story and commitment to praise and commend the efforts and achievements of his colleagues demonstrated the real meaning of trust. He didn’t just tell them that he trusted them, he demonstrated it. Doing this produced tremendous trust among his colleagues and also spread throughout the international network. This shows that great leadership skills and good behavior can also be contagious.





How does this experience illustrate “Strive to Become” and  Stephen Covey's statement that "if we want to make relatively minor changes in our lives, we can perhaps appropriately focus on our attitudes and behaviors. But if we want to make significant, quantum change, we need to work on our basic paradigms"?: To strive is to make purposeful effort. It is to make deliberate, sustained effort, not just casual effort where giving up is easy. When we strive, our efforts are not just experiments, but effort guarded by value and purpose. Henry did not try to build trust by simply attending meetings or giving long talk about trust, instead made a conscious effort to act differently as a leader. His decision to praise and commend the efforts and achievements of his colleagues demonstrated that he believed that shared recognition builds team success. This connects directly to Stephen Covey’s idea about paradigms. Henry’s example did not only help to build trust on the surface level alone, but he helped to build a lasting change in relationships and culture by promoting trust among his colleagues.



What else could Henri have done to continue to “build others” amongst his colleagues and network partners?: He could invest in mentoring. By focusing on having one-on-one interactions and trainings with members of his team would help him identify the strengths and weaknesses of each team member and learn how to help them accordingly.



What does it mean to be a disciple leader?: To be a disciple leader means to follow Jesus Christ and help others do the same. It is the leadership that is focused on serving others and not power or position. A disciple leader corrects others with love, serves them and recognizes that they are not perfect themselves. A disciple leader serves with integrity and purpose, not with pride or demanding of respect or fear from others.



What will you do this semester to become a better disciple of Jesus Christ in the areas of "striving to become" and "building others"?: In the area of “striving to become”, this semester I will prioritize my scripture study and my assignments. I will make sure I plan my daily activities to make out ample time for my studies and submission of assignments.



In the area of “Building others”, I will strive to look for ways that I can use my already existing skills and the skills I will learn in this course to serve others and help them draw closer to Jesus Christ.
feedback:
✅ **Rubric Strengths**:
- You provided a detailed explanation of why Henri's story had a dramatic impact, connecting his actions to building trust and demonstrating contagious leadership.
- You clearly defined "strive to become" as purposeful effort and effectively linked it to Stephen Covey's concept of paradigm shifts.
- You offered a specific, well-explained additional action Henri could take (investing in mentoring) to continue building others.
- You shared a comprehensive definition of a disciple leader, including multiple key characteristics like following Christ, serving others, and leading with integrity.
- You outlined personal, actionable plans for both "striving to become" and "building others" this semester.

⚠️ **Areas for Improvement**:
The grader awarded full points, indicating your submission successfully met all rubric criteria. There are no specific areas requiring correction based on the provided evaluation.

💡 **Guidance**:
Excellent work on this assignment. Your responses demonstrate a strong grasp of the disciple-leadership concepts. To deepen your understanding and application, consider these reflective questions:
1. For your plan to "prioritize scripture study," what specific method or time of day will help you ensure this happens consistently, even during a busy week?
2. In your definition of a disciple leader, you mentioned "correcting others with love." What might be a practical example of offering loving correction in an academic or team setting?
3. You noted that Henri's behavior was "contagious." How can you, in your role as a student, create a similar positive ripple effect within your own circles this semester?

Reflecting on these questions can help you move from understanding these principles to implementing them more fully in your daily life.

My Reflection

Naomi E. A. Alle

Brigham Young University- Idaho

WRIT101.010

Byron Stepherson



Over the past six weeks, I have learned valuable lessons that have strengthened both my writing and confidence as a communicator. One of the main things I learned is how to organize my thoughts more clearly before writing. Creating outlines and drafts helped me logically express ideas, making my writing easier to read and understand. I also learned the importance of writing with a clear purpose and audience in mind. This helped me adjust my tone and word choice depending on whether I was writing a reflection, an essay, or a professional message. Another important lesson was learning how to edit and proofread my work carefully. I realized that strong writing doesn’t happen all at once; it takes revision, feedback, and attention to detail. Lastly, I learned that reflective writing encourages me to connect my personal experiences to what I’m learning, which makes the process more meaningful and enjoyable. 

One of the things I have done well this semester is expressing my thoughts in a way that feels natural and genuine. I have learned to write in my own voice while being professional and clear. Another strength has been my ability to follow directions and apply feedback from assignments. When I received comments about improving transitions or sentence flow, I used them to make my next paper better. I also think I have improved in creating strong introductions and conclusions that capture the main idea and leave a lasting impression. These strengths have helped me become more confident as a writer because I now see writing as a process of growth, not perfection. Each assignment built on the last, and I noticed how my paragraphs became more connected and my points more convincing.

While I have improved a lot, there are still areas I want to work on. One element I hope to strengthen is grammar and punctuation. Sometimes, I make small mistakes that can distract from my message, so I plan to review grammar rules more often and use writing tools like Grammarly to double-check my work. I also want to expand my vocabulary and sentence variety so my writing sounds more engaging and polished. To do this, I plan to read more professional articles and take note of how good writers use language effectively. Finally, I want to continue practicing writing reflections and essays regularly, even outside of class. The more I write, the more confident and skilled I will become.

Overall, this course has taught me that writing is not just about getting words on paper—it’s about expressing thoughts with purpose, learning from feedback, and continually improving. I feel proud of my progress and motivated to keep developing my skills as a thoughtful and effective writer.

Activity: Disciple-Leadership Paper



Answer the following questions about the mini-case and disciple-leadership: 

Why did Henri’s story and subsequent commitment have such a dramatic and immediate impact on the leaders who reported to him?: Henry’s story and commitment to praise and commend the efforts and achievements of his colleagues demonstrated the real meaning of trust. He didn’t just tell them that he trusted them, he demonstrated it. Doing this produced tremendous trust among his colleagues and also spread throughout the international network. This shows that great leadership skills and good behavior can also be contagious.





How does this experience illustrate “Strive to Become” and  Stephen Covey's statement that "if we want to make relatively minor changes in our lives, we can perhaps appropriately focus on our attitudes and behaviors. But if we want to make significant, quantum change, we need to work on our basic paradigms"?: To strive is to make purposeful effort. It is to make deliberate, sustained effort, not just casual effort where giving up is easy. When we strive, our efforts are not just experiments, but effort guarded by value and purpose. Henry did not try to build trust by simply attending meetings or giving long talk about trust, instead made a conscious effort to act differently as a leader. His decision to praise and commend the efforts and achievements of his colleagues demonstrated that he believed that shared recognition builds team success. This connects directly to Stephen Covey’s idea about paradigms. Henry’s example did not only help to build trust on the surface level alone, but he helped to build a lasting change in relationships and culture by promoting trust among his colleagues.



What else could Henri have done to continue to “build others” amongst his colleagues and network partners?: He could invest in mentoring. By focusing on having one-on-one interactions and trainings with members of his team would help him identify the strengths and weaknesses of each team member and learn how to help them accordingly.



What does it mean to be a disciple leader?: To be a disciple leader means to follow Jesus Christ and help others do the same. It is the leadership that is focused on serving others and not power or position. A disciple leader corrects others with love, serves them and recognizes that they are not perfect themselves. A disciple leader serves with integrity and purpose, not with pride or demanding of respect or fear from others.



What will you do this semester to become a better disciple of Jesus Christ in the areas of "striving to become" and "building others"?: In the area of “striving to become”, this semester I will prioritize my scripture study and my assignments. I will make sure I plan my daily activities to make out ample time for my studies and submission of assignments.



In the area of “Building others”, I will strive to look for ways that I can use my already existing skills and the skills I will learn in this course to serve others and help them draw closer to Jesus Christ.
